The P2-bundle model, smoothness/surjectivity/pure relative dimension two, the ordering torsor as a stacky S6-torsor, and domination/dimension formula are supported by the cited ATT-0065/ATT-0066/ATT-0088 chain together with packet findings FND-0134, FND-0139, FND-0142 and the smooth-local stack descent observation in FND-0127. The separate irreducible-component/degree formula over a normal stack is treated under CLM-0096-2.

The proof argues as if V were a normal scheme: it uses that a finite étale cover of a normal scheme is normal and that connected components of a normal locally Noetherian scheme are open and closed. But V is a connected normal component of U, and U is an algebraic stack over the Hurwitz stack H. The attempt gives no smooth-atlas/coarse-space descent, no proof that Z_V→V is representable, and no exclusion of inertia acting on orderings. For a stacky finite étale S6-torsor, the subgroup H_V alone does not automatically yield the stated irreducible-component count and degree |H_V| without controlling stacky inertia or passing to a normal scheme atlas. This leaves clause (2) unresolved.

Pencil recovery is sound on geometric points: O_C(Gamma)≅L, weak normalization gives L≅omega_C(-D), hence omega_C(-Gamma)≅O_C(D)=gamma^*O(1); h^0(O_C(D))=2 by FND-0142, so the pullback H^0(P1,O(1))→H^0(C,O_C(D)) is an isomorphism. This addresses the FND-0137/FND-0098 attack because the recovered pencil is the intrinsic complete linear series |omega_C(-Gamma)|, not an auxiliary chosen subspace.

Given CLM-0096-3, geometric fibres of u have at most one isomorphism class and trivial relative inertia. The standard DM inertia criterion gives representability by algebraic spaces; geometric uniqueness in characteristic zero gives universal injectivity; finite type plus zero-dimensional geometric fibres gives quasi-finiteness; the quasi-finite dimension theorem gives dim closure(u(T))=dim T. This clause does not depend on the unresolved stacky component formula in clause (2).

finding_candidates.statement: For a finite étale S6-ordering torsor Z_V→V over a connected normal algebraic stack V, the scheme-theoretic component formula '[S6:H_V] irreducible components, each of degree |H_V|' is not valid without an additional representability/inertia-free hypothesis or a descent argument through a normal scheme atlas/coarse space controlling stack inertia. Stack inertia can act on the ordered fibre, so monodromy orbits alone do not establish irreducible components or stacky degrees.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack: stack versus coarse/representability in clause (2). H and U are algebraic stacks, not schemes, and the ordered incidence Z→U can inherit stacky stabilizers from automorphisms of the pointed cover. The proof of CLM-0096-2 explicitly uses facts about finite étale covers of normal schemes and then concludes irreducible components and degrees over V from the monodromy subgroup H_V. For a stacky S6-torsor this is not automatic: inertia may act on orderings, the cover need not be representable over V, and the number/degree of irreducible components requires a normal scheme atlas, coarse-space descent, or an explicit inertia-free hypothesis. ATT-0096 supplies none of these. Outcome: the attack succeeds at Pass 1 and makes CLM-0096-2 unresolved. Secondary attacks on pencil recovery, Aut comparison, universal injectivity, and dimension formula fail: the recovery uses the intrinsic complete pencil |omega_C(-Gamma)|, h^0 constancy and weak normalization are packet-corroborated, and the lemma explicitly disclaims Gysin, purity, Tate, closed-immersion, and stable-pair assertions.
theorem_statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Let H be the reduced finite-type algebraic Hurwitz stack whose objects are smooth genus-six finite-flat degree-four covers gamma:C→P of a P1-bundle, modulo isomorphism of the target, satisfying (CE) the standard degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl resolution, (BAL) fibrewise F≅O(4)⊕O(5), and (N) the weak relative-canonical normalization used in ATT-0066 and ATT-0088. No target coordinates, splitting of F, normalization isomorphism, or trivialization of an Abel–Jacobi equality is included as object data. Let W5 be the canonical degree-16 quotient, L=W5⊗omega^{-1}, I the degree-six Abel–Jacobi incidence for L, U⊂I its distinct-support open, and Z=Ord(U) the ordered incidence, equivalently the intrinsic balanced CE evaluation-failure scheme on Conf6. Then: (1) I→H is a P2-bundle, U→H and Z→H are smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two, and Z→U is a finite étale S6-torsor. Every irreducible component T of Z dominates an irreducible component H_alpha of H and dim T=dim H_alpha+2. (2) If V is a connected normal component of U and H_V⊂S6 is the image of the monodromy representation of Z_V→V, then Z_V has exactly [S6:H_V] irreducible components; each is finite étale of degree |H_V| over V and has dimension dim V. (3) The forgetful morphism u:Z→M_{6,6} recovers the tetragonal pencil on every geometric point: for z=(C,gamma,x1,…,x6), with Gamma=sum xi, the complete pencil |omega_C(-Gamma)| is gamma up to a unique target isomorphism. Consequently Aut(C,gamma,x1,…,x6)→Aut(C,x1,…,x6) is an isomorphism, and every geometric fibre of u has either no object or one isomorphism class with trivial relative automorphism group. (4) Hence u is representable by algebraic spaces, universally injective, and quasi-finite. For each irreducible component T⊂Z, dim closure(u(T))=dim T; in particular, if its dominated Hurwitz component has dimension 15, then closure(u(T)) has dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6}. No monomorphism on arbitrary families, closed-immersion, purity, lci, Gysin, or numerical monodromy assertion is made.
